assessment.nobel_worthiness: Opening the neutrino window on the high-energy Universe required a cubic-kilometre detector built in Antarctic ice. IceCube's 2013 detection of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux and the 2017-18 association of a neutrino with the blazar TXS 0506+056 are original, clear and lasting. As an instrument builder in astroparticle physics I regard this as precisely the kind of discovery enabled by a detector that many doubted could work.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and the AMANDA precursor; Karle was a central figure in the detector's construction and operation and in the discovery analyses. The credited pair is a clean two-person configuration, though a large collaboration and other early pioneers (e.g. DUMAND, Baikal) are not in the supplied credit and I cannot verify how others would weigh in.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed with multiple event topologies and by independent analyses; the Galactic-plane neutrino result and NGC 1068 evidence add support. Individual source associations are still maturing, but the core discovery is solid and timely.
uncertainties: Whether the TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 source identifications are viewed as settled enough to be cited in the prize motivation.
Allocation of credit within a very large collaboration and relative to earlier proposers and pioneers of neutrino telescopes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, is a fundamental advance in precision measurement, now reaching fractional uncertainties near 10^-18 and enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. The concept is original and the experimental realisation is as clear and long-lasting as any in modern physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clocks; Jun Ye brought the lattice clock to the highest accuracy and stability and exploited it for many-body physics. The two-name configuration is natural. Other frequency-metrology contributors exist (Hall and Hansch were already honoured in 2005), but they are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories worldwide have reproduced and improved the results with Sr, Yb and others, and international comparisons agree. Timing is good because the redefinition of the second is under active discussion.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for trapped-ion control.
How much credit should go to other lattice-clock groups and to ion-clock developers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope images of M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022) used a planet-sized VLBI array at 230 GHz to resolve the shadow of a black hole directly. It is a landmark instrument achievement with clear scientific meaning, and the 2020 prize recognised the existence of black holes but not this direct imaging.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the building of the global array and the technical demonstrations, and Moran was foundational in submillimetre VLBI. The credited three are plausible, but the 2019 result was the work of a very large collaboration and the roles of other leaders are contested in public discussion.
assessment.maturity: Both images are consistent with general relativity and with independent polarisation and multi-epoch data; the M87* ring has reappeared across years. Independent confirmation by a different array is still pending, so the maturity is good but not complete.
uncertainties: Lack of an independent instrument confirming the images; calibration and image-reconstruction systematics.
Credit allocation within a collaboration of hundreds, and the extent to which the 2020 prize for black holes lessens novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall effect and three-dimensional topological insulators created a whole class of topological matter with protected surface states. The originality and lasting influence are very high and the field has produced materials and ideas used well beyond condensed matter. This is outside my own expertise, so I rely on colleagues for fine judgments.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele predicted the quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe quantum wells (following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, who are not in the credit); Hasan's group observed 3D topological insulators in Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3. I choose Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan to cover theory, 2D experiment and 3D experiment, but Mele's equal role in the Kane-Mele paper makes this allocation contentious.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed by many groups with ARPES, transport and related experiments across several materials; the field is mature, and recognition is timely, even somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Fair exclusion of Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and other contributors such as Moore and Balents, Fu and Kane.
Whether the committee views this discovery as the first of several (including the quantum anomalous Hall effect) that need to be considered as a unit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic oscillation scale provides a standard ruler imprinted in the galaxy distribution, and its first detections in 2005 by SDSS and 2dFGRS turned the large-scale structure into a precise tool for measuring dark energy and expansion history. It is a clear and durable observational achievement relying on large survey instruments.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein led the SDSS luminous-red-galaxy detection; Cole and Peacock were leading members of the 2dFGRS analysis that showed the same feature. The list omits the theoretical originators (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) and other survey leaders, and I cannot verify how credit would be shared.
assessment.maturity: Independent detection in 2dFGRS and SDSS, later confirmed by WiggleZ, BOSS and DESI, which reinforces the interpretation. Tension in recent DESI results in dark-energy modelling does not affect the existence of the feature.
uncertainties: Competing candidates for credit in the theory and in survey leadership.
Whether the committee regards this primarily as a tool rather than as a discovery per se, particularly while cosmological interpretation is under active debate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers produce femtosecond, coherent, extremely bright X-ray pulses that enabled serial femtosecond crystallography, ultrafast structural dynamics and other new experiments. As a detector and instrument developer I value this as a major accelerator-based invention that opened measurements previously impossible.
assessment.attribution: The SASE concept and its realisation involve Pellegrini, Kim and Rossbach (FLASH/TESLA, and theory with Saldin, Schneidmiller and Yurkov, and Bonifacio, who are not in the supplied credit). Allocation is genuinely difficult because LCLS and the Hamburg groups, as well as theory, each had pivotal contributors.
assessment.maturity: Operating facilities (FLASH, LCLS, SACLA, European XFEL) have confirmed the technology and generated large science output; the invention is mature though the Nobel question concerns whether the inventions are physics discoveries or engineering achievements.
uncertainties: Unresolved and contested attribution among accelerator-physics pioneers.
Whether the committee wants to recognise the tool or the science it enabled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing array evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background (2023) opens a new window on supermassive-black-hole binaries or early-Universe physics, using the Galaxy as a detector. It is a significant new observational window, building on decades of precision pulsar timing.
assessment.attribution: The decisive work is by multiple collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA); the supplied credit points to leaders of the programmes rather than to the particular analysis, which makes a fair three-person prize difficult, and I cannot verify who would be judged decisive.
assessment.maturity: Premature: the evidence is at roughly 3 to 4 sigma with no definitive Hellings-Downs confirmation across independent arrays and no source identification. The interpretation as supermassive black-hole binaries is not settled.
uncertainties: Statistical significance and the alternative sources of the signal.
Attribution across several competing collaborations and countries.
Whether waiting for a clear detection and anisotropy or individual sources is wiser.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable moire system and founded twistronics. Its originality is clear and it has influenced a huge number of works; my own expertise is not in this area, so I defer to the colleagues here.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered the correlated and superconducting states in 2018. This theory-and-experiment pairing is a natural configuration, though other contributors such as Dean, Young and Efetov, and Santos and Castro Neto might be argued for.
assessment.maturity: The key phenomena were reproduced by several independent groups, but the underlying mechanism of superconductivity and device sample variability are still being studied, so it may be early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and sample-to-sample reproducibility are unresolved.
Allocation of credit among theorists and the experimental groups.
